reviews.codex: ran-no-findings (Codex environment lacked shell access; manual walkthrough of S3 additions confirmed correctness)

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The Codex review backend ran successfully but could not inspect the working tree because command execution is unavailable in the Codex review environment, returning a zero-finding non-result rather than an actionable review. This required falling back to manual code inspection for the mandatory review gate.
retrospective.surprised_by: The mandatory review infrastructure produced a structurally valid but content-free result due to a Codex sandbox constraint (no shell access). A prior architect run also crashed before writing result.json despite a clean implementation — the two back-to-back crashes on the finalization step (not the implementation step) suggest the review + artifact-writing tail of the pipeline is a recurring fragility point.

lead_clarifications.question: Examiner flagged #messagesByEpoch unbounded growth (sev 5): entries older than currentEpoch-snapshotDepth are dead but never pruned — a memory leak in long-lived groups.
lead_clarifications.answer: Lead added #pruneMessagesByEpoch(floor) helper called at all 3 snapshot-prune sites (selfUpdate, commit, ingest), bounding the map to snapshotDepth. All 475 tests pass; build clean. Dead entries (no surviving snapshot to roll back to) are now pruned alongside snapshots.
